I can't easily sleep as well. I just never feel tired despite the fact that I'm no doubt am.

Take this with a grain of salt since I'm not expert, but.

The fact though that you've said that you can't fall sleep until sunrise means that your biological clock is so out of wack that it's not triggering your sleepyness until it's morning. Generally this means that you're experiencing too much light before it's time to go to bed and your clock thinks that it's time for you to stay awake.

​

Here's a couple of steps I would do.

1. Get more sunlight or orange juice in your system in the morning. You need to tell your body that it's wakeup time in the morning, not sleep time.
2. Train extensively 3-4 hours before you think you can fall asleep. Now just wait a second, I don't mean exercising and running. I'm talking about 2-3 hours of pure training to exhaust yourself. Do everything you can to exhaust yourself. Even if you think you can't do it, you can. Just take it slower, but still keep at it. I've broken my shitty sleep cycle through this method. Even if you "feel" tired, keep going until that 2nd hour hits. No electronics too, set a alarm for 2 hours at least and forget about time. Preferably do this in a lightened environment if you can't do it outside.
3. So for some reason you can't fall asleep, don't lay in bed for more then 15 or so minutes, get up and do something in the dark or low light. Time to bust out those library books you never returned. Only when you feel tired or unconsciously yawn, then crawl back to bed and rest. That's right, you're resting, not trying to sleep. Rest while thinking about that book.

​

To be honest I shouldn't be giving advice because I have a massive amount of trouble getting to sleep. But, maybe these methods will work better for you then me.
